correctness.rationale: Exact negative-binomial identity yields a_r,k=(r C(r+k-1,k)/r^k-1)/(r-1). The coefficient sequence declines strictly after k=1 and tends to zero, so d_r exists and is the first strictly negative coefficient. L^k_uv=0 for k<dist(u,v); L^d_uv=(-1)^d times the sum of positive weighted graph geodesics. Their signs cancel with the analytic coefficient and yield strict small-step negativity at distance d_r in every graph of sufficient diameter. Laplacian spectral diagonalization gives T_r(h)->11^T/n>0 entrywise, proving eventual recovery. For k=(1±eps)log r/loglog r, log product(1+j/r)=O(k²/r)=o(1), and Stirling provides the sharp d_r ratio limit. The included exact-rational verifier reconstructs an explicit P5 matrix counterexample and correct finite coefficient transitions; no infinite assertion rests solely on code.

value.rationale: Accuracy acceleration through a negative-weight Richardson combination can destroy the discrete maximum principle on undirected physical diffusion networks at arbitrarily small timestep, despite each implicit Euler constituent preserving positivity and despite eventual recovery. For every integer refinement count this gives an exact structural distance certificate in terms of the edge-weight geodesic sum and a surprisingly slow log r/loglog r improvement, informing whether additional substeps can protect spatial positivity. This is a meaningful all-refinement geometric obstruction, not a numeric recomputation or renaming of the known scalar large-step sign boundary. It does not claim a complete phase diagram or a minimal arbitrary-step failing graph size.
